newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU real farm prices down 2.7 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU real farm prices down 2.7 percent in 1996.

text.p: The index of farm producer prices in the European Union fell 2.7 percent in real terms in 1996, ending the stability seen in 1994 and 1995, the EU's statistics office Eurostat said on Wednesday.
The index rose 0.2 percent over 1995 in nominal terms, but that translated into a real drop of 3.9 percent for crop products and 1.5 percent for animals and animal products, it said in a report.
"The real output price index, which was 100 in 1990, reached 83.3 in 1996," it said.
Among the 15 EU countries, the steepest falls were in Finland (14.8 percent), Ireland (6.5 percent), Luxembourg (5 percent), Sweden (4.6 percent) and Spain and Britain (3.9 percent).
The report said the index of purchase prices for goods and services used by farmers in the EU had risen in 1996 by 3.9 percent in nominal terms and 1.2 percent in real terms.

It said prices for energy and lubricants had increased 4.6 percent, animal feedingstuffs 2.6 percent and fertilisers 2 percent. Overall investment costs changed little from 1995, however, with a 1.2 percent price rise for machinery offset by a 1.2 percent decrease for buildings.
